title: Hazel and the Homes
markdown:
The late afternoon sun cast honey-rose shadows across Mr. Kellan’s garden. Hazel, hands smudged with sawdust, hummed as she polished a little wooden birdhouse. Beside her, Fizz the ferret tumbled with an autumn leaf.

Kellan peered over his spectacles. “Our pond neighbors seem a trifle misplaced this evening.”

Fizz stopped, head cocked. “Misplaced?” Hazel set down the birdhouse.

“Little Froggy looked sad. Glyn Beetle seemed unsure where to burrow. Flutter the Moth fluttered uncertainly as twilight crept in.”

Fizz’s ears twitched. “Lost homes? Everyone needs a cozy one.”

“Perhaps the right home. Safe and sound. Sometimes that takes exploring.” He gestured toward the whispering woods.

Their expedition was a slow amble. “Look.” Hazel pointed to a grand oak. Squirrels darted up the bark. “Nests in the hollows. The woods suit them.”

Fizz sniffed. “Pine needles and damp earth. Lovely for me. A bit dry and leafy for Froggy.”

They ambled to the shimmering pond. A chorus of contented croaks. Froggy, hopping beside them, sighed and splashed. “Cool water. Tall reeds. Yummy wriggly flies.”

“The pond is right for you,” Hazel said. “Water, food, rest.”

A solid Glyn Beetle scurried from under a fallen leaf. “Lovely pond. A bit too wet. I prefer soft warm earth.”

“The meadow beyond the ferns,” Kellan said. “Soil for burrowing.”

They led him to the edge. Glyn burrowed, happy surprise. “Room to tunnel. Sweet roots. A beetle’s place.”

A gentle shadow drifted. Flutter landed on a tall moon-white flower. “The meadow is comforting. I rest among flowers — nectar, soft petals. The garden is my favourite.”

Hazel looked from Froggy splashing, to Glyn snug in earth, to Flutter on her flower. “Everyone needs a place that’s right. Safe. What they need.”

Kellan named it once: habitat. Food, water, shelter, room. Like Hazel’s workshop. Like Fizz’s nook by the hearth.

Fizz yawned, a wide stretch. “And I have my people.” He nudged her hand.

The sun dipped. Shy stars. The pond settled into its watery world. They walked toward the cottage glow. Hazel whispered that it felt good to help. Kellan only nodded. Back in the workshop Fizz curled by the stove. Hazel tidied her tools. Kellan watched the moon. The birdhouse, finished, waited for someone whose home was air and twigs, not pond or meadow or nectar.
